The user data of the log or trace message shall be represented by DltArguments that are ordered in the DltMessage .
If the argument contains only static text, this text shall be placed in the DESC element of the DltArgument . In this case the DltArgument . length shall be set to zero.

If the argument contains n on - s tatic d ata , the data trans ported in the message is described by the DltArgument . length and by the aggregated networkRepresentation that defines the unit and the baseType.
The timer shall start with ‘00000000’ when the ECU which generates the LogMessage starts up.
The Dlt module shall be able to buffer data coming from calls to Dlt_SendLogMessage and/or Dlt_SendTraceMessage even if the Dlt module has not been initialized yet.

As soon as the Dlt module is initialized by Dlt_Init and the optional timer DltGeneralStartUpDelayTimer has expired, all the log and trace data, which has been buffered meanwhile, shall be processed according to [SWS_Dlt_00651], using the configured filter settings.
The Dlt module shall remember the relation between the registered tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId , and the port interface where this tuple is registered.
Port defined argument values shall be used by the Dlt module as SessionIds.
The port defined argument value corresponds to the defined SessionID. The value shall start at 0x1000 (for BSW modules the module ID is taken).

The Dlt module shall provide the implementation of the hook functions for every configured event given by an BswModuleEntry, which owns a shortName starting with "Rte_Dlt" provided by the BswModuleDefinition of the RTE.
MessageIds used for DEM ( 0x00000001 ) and DET ( 0x00000002 ), and Trace Messages ( 0x00000003 ) are reserved and therefore not usable for SW-Cs.

The Dlt module shall provide the possibility to trace all kinds of trace events described in the SWS RTE.
In the hook function the internal representation of Dlt_SendTraceMessage shall be called. This call shall be in non-verbose mode.
The payload for this hook function call shall be filled with the arguments provided by the hook function. All data transported with the arguments shall be provided.
Every hook function shall get its own DltSwcContextId . In some cases some events can be bundled to the same ContextId. This shall mostly be done if a very large number of signals are traced.
Because non-verbose mode is used, a unique Message ID as defined in [SWS_Dlt_00031] shall be used for each call to Dlt_SendTraceMessage .

Dlt shall use for every VFB trace hook function an own DltSwcContextId and thus handle for every VFB trace DltSwcContextId a separate trace status. This can be done with a separate variable.

The prototype of this hook function is to be taken from the Bsw ModuleEntry of the BSWModuleDescription of the RTE.

If the Dlt command Dlt_SetTraceStatus is requested, but the addressed tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId is unknown, the Dlt command shall be answered with DLT_E_ERROR .

If the Dlt command Dlt_GetLogInfo is requested, but the addressed tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId is unknown, the Dlt command shall be answered with DLT_E_ERROR .
If the Dlt command Dlt_GetDefaultLogLevel is requested, the current value of the parameter DltDefaultLogLevel shall be returned.

If the Dlt command Dlt_ResetToFactoryDefault is requested and if the parameter DltGeneralNvRAMSupport is set to FALSE , E_OK shall be returned if the Dlt module reset the current configuration values to the default configuration successfully.

If the Dlt command Dlt_ResetToFactoryDefault is requested and the parameter DltGeneralNvRAMSupport is set to TRUE , response with "ERROR" • if the Dlt module could not reset the current configuration to the static default configuration or • if the stored configuration of the NvM could not be deleted.
If the Dlt command Dlt_SetDefaultLogLevel is requested, the parameter DltDefaultLogLevel shall be updated to the received newLogLevel .
If the Dlt command Dlt_SetDefaultTraceStatus is requested, the parameter DltDefaultTraceStatus shall be updated to the received newTraceStatus
If the Dlt command Dlt_GetDefaultTraceStatus is requested, the current value of the parameter DltDefaultTraceStatus shall be returned.
If the Dlt command Dlt_GetLogChannelNames is requested, the number of configured LogChannels and requested number of LogChannel names given by the parameter DltLogChannelName shall be returned.
If the Dlt Command Dlt_GetTraceStatus is requested, the DltLogTraceStatusFlag shall be returned for the received tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId .

If the Dlt command Dlt_SetLogChannelAssignment is requested with parameter addRemoveOp set to DLT_ASSIGN_ADD , add the tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId to the LogChannel with the name provided by the parameter logChannelName . The Dlt command shall return E_OK even if the tuple was already assigned to the requested LogChannel before.

If the Dlt command Dlt_SetLogChannelAssignment is requested with parameter addRemoveOp set to DLT_ASSIGN_REMOVE , remove the tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId from the LogChannel with the name provided by the parameter logChannelName . The Dlt command shall return E_OK even if the tuple was not assigned to the requested LogChannel before.
If the Dlt command Dlt_SetLogChannelAssignment is requested with an unknown tuple of DltSwcApplicationId / DltSwcContextId or an unknown LogChannel name, the Dlt command shall return DLT_E_ERROR .
If the Dlt command Dlt_SetLogChannelThreshold is requested, the DltLogChannelThreshold of the addressed LogChannel shall be set to the value received by the parameter newThreshold
If the Dlt command Dlt_SetLogChannelThreshold is requested and the logChannelName and/or the newThreshold is unknown, the Dlt command shall return DLT_E_ERROR .
If the Dlt command Dlt_GetLogChannelThreshold is requested, the DltLogChannelThreshold of the addressed LogChannel shall be returned.
If the Dlt command Dlt_GetLogChannelThreshold is requested and the logChannelName or the logChannelThreshold is unknown, the Dlt command shall return DLT_E_ERROR .
